correctness.rationale: For scalar kernels k_n(t)=b^n exp(-b^n t), Minkowski/Tonelli and near-Dirac positive-time inputs prove exact operator norm sup_{norm(v)_r=1} integral norm_r((k_n(u)v_n)) du, not just a bound on a test vector. For finite r set a_n=|v_n|^r on simplex; r=infinity maximizing coordinates have absolute value one. Logarithmic intervals (b^-j,b^{1-j}] turn the norm into shifted sums v_{n-j}(w)=b^{n-j} exp(-b^{n-j}w); truncated |k|<=K tails integrate to eta<=b^-K+exp(-b^{K+1}), via telescoping e^-b^k. Uniform a_n=1/N on N-2K center scales gives lower bound; Hölder across at most N+2K populated scales and the sum a_n=1 give matching upper; dividing by N^{1-1/r} gives claimed explicit error. For b↓1, shifted Riemann sums of G_r(x)=exp(rx-r exp x) yield Gamma(r)/r^r and coefficient Gamma(r)^{1/r}/r*(log b)^{1-1/r}; for r=infinity sampled sup exp(x-exp x) has max 1/e, and b→infinity selecting adjacent kernels yields kappa→1. Independently computed kappa_2(2)=0.416277305367437044167102342 with 70 summands and mpmath quadrature, matching claimed 18 digits; numerical integration alone does not prove norm asymptotics.
residual_risks: The asymptotic holds at fixed b>1 as N→infinity; no uniform b→1,N→infinity claim or stochastic generalization.
